name: Dynamic Volume Raycasting with Accumulated Shading
definition: A raycasting technique that renders a dynamic volume composed of overlapping spherical sources (balls). It uses a compute shader to update a 3D texture field representing density and color, then uses a pixel shader to march rays through the volume, applying a transfer function for opacity and accumulating color using front-to-back blending with early ray termination.
summary: Dynamic Volume Raycasting with Accumulated Shading is a GPU technique that renders overlapping spherical sources in a single pass using dynamic branching and early termination.
